profile.campus: Data4 Warsaw campus, Jawczyce, Poland (WAW1 and WAW2, combined ~4 hectares / 60 MW per Data4 own site)
profile.reading: This Data4 facility, coded WAW1, is located at Przyparkowa 21, 05-850 Jawczyce, Poland, roughly 20 minutes from central Warsaw, on a campus the operator own page also lists as home to a second building, WAW2. The operator own page gives combined campus totals of approximately 4 hectares and 60 MW of available IT power but does not break these figures down by individual building, so no building specific capacity or square footage is attributed to this record. Data4 is a data center operator founded in 2006 and headquartered in Paris, France, operating campuses in France, Italy, Spain, Poland, Germany, and Greece. Data4 was founded in 2006 and is headquartered in Paris, France, described in the company own 2019-era published materials as controlled by AXA, the French insurance and asset-management group, though the specific AXA entity and any co-investors could not be independently confirmed this session. Data4 own site describes a six-country European footprint spanning France, Italy, Spain, Poland, Germany, and Greece, totaling roughly ten campuses, 1.5 gigawatts of capacity, and 165,000 square meters of IT space group-wide. Jawczyce sits roughly 20 minutes outside central Warsaw, and Poland has grown as a significant Central European data center market in recent years, driven by strong fiber connectivity and EU digital infrastructure investment, factors consistent with Data4 decision to establish a two-building campus there as one of its newer European markets. The Warsaw campus sits alongside Data4 broader Central and Eastern European ambitions, an area of growing hyperscale and enterprise demand as cloud providers seek to serve the region without routing traffic through Western Europe, and Poland own digital economy has grown quickly enough in recent years that multiple international operators beyond Data4 have also established or expanded data center campuses in the Warsaw metro area during the same period.
